citation: Rosén LA, Silva LOB, Andersson UK et al. (2009). Endosperm and whole grain rye breads are characterized by low post-prandial insulin response and a beneficial blood glucose profile. Nutrition Journal 8:42-42.
protocol: Eight breakfast cereals in a crossover, each 40 g available starch (porridges ~38 g): white wheat bread reference (1.8 g fibre) vs endosperm rye bread (6.7 g), whole-grain rye bread (9.6 g), rye bran bread (12.3 g) and matching porridges. Capillary and venous blood at 0, 7.5, 15, 30, 45, 70, 95, 120, 180 min.
population: n=12 healthy volunteers (9 men, 3 women), age 25.3 ± 0.8 y, BMI 23.1 ± 0.6 kg/m2.

reports.where: Table 4: incremental peak, iAUC 0-30, iAUC 0-120, GI per meal
Table 5: incremental peak, iAUC 0-30, iAUC 0-120, II per meal

note: Paired-meal contrast, fibre: white wheat bread vs whole-grain / endosperm / bran rye breads and porridges at matched available starch. Several whole-against-refined grain steps on the same people, so a dose of cereal fibre. Watch: fat and protein differ slightly (1.1-2.6 g fat, 4.6-9.7 g protein), blood glucose n=11 and insulin n=12, some rows are index values relative to the reference. Only in figures: time courses.
